climate.koppen_name: Cold, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Seasons this mild ripen Riesling, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon fully without cooking off their freshness.
Riesling, Pinot Noir and Chardonnay sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Pinot Gris is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.

soil.rock: Shale and mudstone are fine-grained rocks that hold heat well and are moderately fertile.
soil.top: The topsoil drains fast and warms early in spring. Vines get little water, which keeps crops small and flavors concentrated, but drought bites hard. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: Mostly flat. Easy and cheap to farm by machine, but on still nights cold air settles on flat ground, so spring frost is a bigger risk.
